card.one_sentence: Storefront product-page contract is the purchase-facing expression rule under which each Card 1 live offer has a canonical product page that consumes Card 2's closed claim gate, exposes product selection and cart-add affordances, and stops before inferring transaction, provenance, policy-publication, accessibility, admin, or source-revision facts.
card.why_this_shape: One coordinate captures shared ownership, required inputs, core purchase expression, and stop rules while four product-specific suffixes and optional-section configurations remain variants rather than duplicated semantic objects.

map_worthiness.granularity_result: one semantic object with four product-specific variants
map_worthiness.reason: distinct task noun; owns durable purchase-expression rule; changes independently; clear boundaries; spans authority, topology, and public observations; answers declared cold-reader question

shape.rule: One observed canonical product route per Card 1 live offer; ghosts receive no purchasable expression under this contract.
Title, media, selection controls, availability expression, quantity, and add-to-cart affordance.
Names, membership, and contents come only from Card 1, never stale theme copy.

Benefit, proof, FAQ, testimonial or review, shipping, return, and guarantee language must pass Card 2's closed gate; current live deviations remain known_nonconforming until corrected and re-observed.
Bundle, Solo, Legacy, and Spare Spikes use dedicated semantic suffixes and a shared core; optional how-to, media or proof, founder, FAQ, review, and recommendation sections vary by offer.
Product-data binding and cart-add forms are required; successful cart and checkout are separate verification surfaces.
Preserve public route, canonical path, exposed suffix, public theme marker, observation date, and evidence limits; local code alone is insufficient.
